observations.label: Gentle clearing and difficult light · 2:43
observations.text: He reports trying hand movements to reveal fine particles without moving them away. Yellow light made recognition difficult. This is a reported experience, not a tested recovery method.

observations.text: He predicts fine gold in clay, then reports no find yet at 5:25. Keep the prediction separate from that negative result; clay alone did not confirm gold.

science.title: Gold
science.publisher: Harold Kirkemo, William L. Newman and Roger P. Ashley · U.S. Geological Survey
science.note: Explains gold's high density and concentration on or near bedrock as moving stream sediment is agitated during high water. General process guidance, not a prediction for an individual crevice. Primary text inspected; HTTP 200 confirmed after an initial automated-access block.

science.title: Descriptive model of Placer Au–PGE · Model 39a
science.note: Describes gold concentrations associated with fractured bedrock, natural riffles, basal gravel and gravel above clay layers. The model describes deposit settings; it does not verify any diagrammed trap. Primary text inspected; HTTP 200 confirmed after an initial automated-access block.

science.title: Gold Panning · 2018 revision · printed page 8
science.publisher: U.S. Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management
science.note: Identifies bedrock crevices, pockets, downstream sides of boulders and impermeable clay contacts as candidate sampling settings. This is a Kenai Peninsula guide; its access rules and seasonal advice are not transferred to New England. PDF text and HTTP availability checked.

safety.title: Cold Water Hazards and Safety
safety.note: Cold shock can disrupt breathing before hypothermia develops. Dress for water temperature, use appropriate flotation and leave the water if conditions exceed your preparation. Full page inspected.

safety.title: River and Stream Safety
safety.note: Warns about currents beneath calm-looking surfaces, slippery rocks, narrow gaps, strainers and rapidly changing water levels. These hazards apply to observation as well as collection. Primary text and HTTP availability checked.

safety.title: Title 38, §480-Q · Gold panning and motorized recreational gold prospecting
safety.note: The gold-panning exemption has conditions, including no stream-bank disturbance or unlicensed discharge. Motorized prospecting has separate conditions and closures. This is not blanket permission for crevicing, suction devices or any particular site. Current statute text and HTTP availability checked; confirm method and site with the responsible agency.

safety.title: Recreational Gold Prospecting · hand-method guidance
safety.publisher: Maine Land Use Planning Commission · form revised October 2020
safety.note: For LUPC-jurisdiction waters, the guidance describes conditional hand-method exemptions, landowner permission, protecting banks and habitat, and restoring disturbed river-bottom sediment. Its geographic scope is limited; ask LUPC about your exact method and site. PDF text inspected.

safety.title: River Management · Mineral Prospecting
safety.note: Vermont distinguishes hand panning, permitted sluices and prohibited suction dredges, and requires written permission on private land. Maine permissions do not carry across a state boundary. Current primary text and HTTP availability checked; confirm the proposed tools before use.
